script.base: Seattle is the side the book expects to lead (implied 24.5 to 17.0 on a 41.5 total). Base flow is a moderate-pace outdoor game, not a shootout: SEA is ahead by about a score at half and finishes on the ground with Kenneth Walker if Zach Charbonnet (Doubtful, foot) sits, against a Saints run defense that has allowed 4.52 YPC and 6 runs of 10+. New Orleans, as a 7.5-point dog, falls behind and throws (Olave 23 targets, Johnson 20, Shaheed 14 through two games) while Alvin Kamara's carries dry up.
script.flip1: The depleted Seattle secondary (Witherspoon, Love, Emmanwori all Doubtful) plus Chase Young out keeps New Orleans in it or ahead. Seattle never gets the clock-kill, so Walker's late carries stall, and Kamara stays in a neutral run script long enough that a 99-yard type game can clear 72.5. This is the flip that loses both legs.
script.flip2: It becomes a real blowout (spread is already 7.5, so a blowout flag is on). If SEA is up big, Walker may have the yards early but late snaps are at risk; Kamara's rush under gets safer as NO abandons the run. The other blowout version — NO scores first and SEA trails — kills the Walker rush over the way a trailing back's rushing line dies, and is the less likely flip given the 24.5/17.0 script.

matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Walker, the efficient back (125 yards on 23 carries, 5.43 YPC) whose carry share should rise if Charbonnet sits, into NO's 4.52 YPC run defense, in a favorite-leads script. The inverse overlap is Kamara (144 yards on 32 carries, but a 45/99 split) running into SEA's 3.51 YPC front — he attacks the strength, not the weakness. NO's primary pass options (Olave 23 targets/219 air/only 108 yards; Johnson 20/125/144 air) do overlap a left-side YPA bleed and three Doubtful coverage players, but there is no alignment chart, SEA rarely blitzes (where NO's EPA is actually negative), and the Saints' own OL injuries fight the deep-shot overlap. That passing overlap is noted and not bet. JSN (23 targets, 227 yards, 281 air) overlaps NO's middle bleed and a missing Young, but he is illness-Questionable and the favorite script is run-leaning, so that overlap is also not bet.

pro_edge.script_read: Spread 7.5 is past the 3.5 flag: the dog (NO) should throw more, so WR/TE/RB targets rise if they trail, and the leader (SEA) should run late, so the lead RB's carries rise. A 7.5 spread is a moderate blowout flag, not a 14-point laugher, so starter snap risk is real only if it gets out of hand. Total 41.5 is not a high-total volume-over environment; it leans run-heavy for the favorite and against a shootout stack. Team volume, not raw averages, is the usage base: SEA has about 27 rush attempts per game (Charbonnet 27, Walker 23, Barner 2, Darnold 2 over two games).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Charbonnet was only Doubtful and played, Walker stayed in the 20-yard committee split, and the 105 was the fluke; or Seattle trailed and the clock-kill never came, which the 7.5 number does not forbid. On Kamara, the counter-case is almost as strong as the read: a two-game 3.51 YPC sample, an unresolved Penning/Fuaga tag, and one explosive like the 99-yard game clear 72.5 in a close first half before New Orleans ever abandons the run. Weather we do not have, or a 90-minute inactive reversal, would also explain a miss. The counter is not stronger than the Walker role-change read, so that leg stays flagged rather than cut; it is strong enough on Kamara that this lean must not be sized and dies if the OL questionables are full and the total moves up.
slip_story: One story only: Seattle leads and runs the clock. Walker rush over is the lead-back carry absorption after a Doubtful Charbonnet; Kamara rush under is the dog abandoning the run into a good front. They win together. Do not add JSN, Olave, Kupp, or Johnson overs — those need pass volume or a shootout and fight the 41.5 total and the Walker clock-kill — and do not pair a game-total under with any same-game pass-catcher over. No TD legs, one market per player, two legs. This is a pre-kick story log, not a slip to place.
